result:
Both solutions give the same final answer, $p^n + p - 1$, and they rest on the same assumption: that the three subgroups have orders $p-1$, $p^{n-1}$, and $p^{n-1}(p-1)$.

The arithmetic checks out. Since $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ is cyclic of order $p^{n-1}(p-1)$ for odd $p$, it has a unique subgroup of each divisor order, so the orders listed are well-defined. The sum is $p^{n-1} + (p-1) + p^{n-1}(p-1) = p^n + p - 1$.

The weak point is the identification of the three subgroups, which neither solution justifies. The problem asserts there are exactly three, and neither solution derives which ones. I can't confirm from memory which three subgroups appear in the classification of almost commutative Terwilliger algebras for cyclic $p$-groups, so the choice of orders is unverified for both.

Solution A is slightly more explicit about the structure (p-part, p'-part, full group). That gives it a marginal edge in presentation, though not in verified correctness. The two are effectively tied.

WINNER: A
